title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

**APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE**

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.”

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

What you’ll do

What is printmaking? We invite you into our print studio to experience a fun beginner’s journey through this incredible art form in five paced weeks. Join Kelly in this unique introduction to print through the world of monotype, relief, intaglio and stencil screenprinting. This popular multi-session workshop is only taught twice per year in the spring and fall seasons. Students will try various techniques in this guided, hands-on class to create a beginning portfolio of prints. Learn a basic understanding of the four classic methods within the family of printmaking and gain access to our member’s print studio to continue working on your own projects. This class is perfect for absolute beginners or even experienced artists who may need a refresher course in printmaking.

Monotype – Create a single print on a flat matrix using ink and a variety of marks and  textures

Relief – Carve, ink and block print using a mini speedy carve block and a linocut tool

Intaglio – Draw, scratch and ink onto a surface to roll out a creative print using a small press

Stencil – Pull a silkscreen and learn to transfer a flat stencil to make a colorful printed impression

No prior printmaking experience is necessary. This class requires hand dexterity to maneuver carving tools and studio equipment. Students must feel comfortable handling machinery.

title: Morning Yoga
description: Regenerative Ayurvedic Yoga with Tirza Dawn Come, step onto your mat with an open heart and an open mind. Invest in your self care and join us for morning yoga in the OCA studio. $20 per class, $15 for OCA members. Each Wednesday from 9:00-10:15 AM in our Studio. Pay at the door for a-la-carte sessions or use the links below to pay ahead for four weeks at a time.  Pay Online 4 sessions - OCA members  Pay Online 4 sessions - non members Tirza Dawn Naramore is a yogi, mother, artist, ceremonialist and lover of life. She has been practicing and teaching yoga and meditation for 30 years and offers yoga retreats and trainings that center on optimum health, self realization and self love. Her teachers are from many yoga and tantric traditions, but her primary lineages are Iyengar and Kali Ray.  Tirza is deeply devoted to community building and is honored to have created a number of community supported non profits including Mystic Family Circus and The AWAKEN Project, which serves families with children on the autism spectrum. Tirza is proud to be the mother of 3 wild teenagers, including her incredible son who is diagnosed with autism. Tirza's spirituality is one of many influences and teachings. Beginning with a Christian up-bringing and being raised on a Christian commune in her early childhood, she later expanded into more earth-based ways. While in her 20's Tirza was adopted into the Native American Church, where she learned from her relatives a way of living the "Beauty Way." During the 1990's and early 2000's, Tirza lived in San Francisco, Oakland and Berkeley, directing the Mystic Family Circus, which was a performance group dedicated to cultural awareness and bridge building. She worked with Cirque du Soleil, Burning Man, Reclaiming, Contraband, CELLspace and other Bay Area art collectives and non profits to provide conscious entertainment and "prayerformances" for the betterment of humankind and the planet. In 2012, Tirza helped to found the Buckeye Gathering, an ancestral skills gathering in Northern California which draws teachers and students of all ages to learn ancestral ways of tending the earth and survival skills. Tirza Dawn was the founder of yoga programming and the Ayurvedic Yoga Teacher Trainings at the dhyana Center of Ayurveda in Sebastopol, California, which operated a community center of healing and education from 2010 to 2020.

title: What About Age? Art Exhibit
description:
*What About Age?* art exhibit has arrived in Marin County! Originally displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows, this exhibit explores ageism through contemporary art, featuring works by both local youth and senior artists.

*What About Age?* is an art exhibit and educational initiative designed to challenge stereotypes about aging, address ageism and social isolation, and promote intergenerational dialogue through the lens of art.

In partnership with Youth in Arts, the exhibit features artworks by local youth and senior artists, showcasing how age intersects with creativity, identity, and experience. Under the guidance of Youth in Arts, these emerging and established artists work side by side to create collaborative pieces, fostering meaningful connections between generations and reflecting the exhibit’s core message: art is ageless.

The exhibit also includes artwork panels by New York-based writer and illustrator Aubrey Hirsch, first displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows and originally organized by Stacey Gordon, NYU’s Program Director of Next Phase Adult Caregiving and Retirement at Work Life.

The new exhibition will be on view at the Marin County Civic Center galleries from January 26 to May 6, 2026. Works will be displayed on the first and third floor exhibits, Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

The *What About Age?* art exhibit is presented by Marin Cultural Association in partnership with Marin Community Foundation and Youth in Arts. Beyond the art exhibit, the *What About Age?* initiative offers programming, led by Vivalon, designed to challenge ageism and provide resources for Marin County's growing aging population.

title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

**APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE**

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.”

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Coordinated Entry Advisory Committee Meeting April 1, 2026
S.R. Laws
description:
S.R. LAWS IS OUT THERE: He approaches songwriting with a passion for songs that we all grew up on. His sound rings a familiar bell in your head while still delivering ideas completely unique.  He draws inspiration from outstanding storytellers like John Hiatt, Lou Reed, Steve Earle, Neil Finn and Ron Sexsmith. All of their music and others have carved a deep groove.

Growing up out there in Northern California, he developed a unique connection to music early on. His father worked as a trash collector, and he would spend hours sifting through bags of discarded 45 records. Each find felt like stumbling upon hidden treasures. Some records were covered in dirt and grime, while others were pristine. The thrill of discovering new sounds was exhilarating, and he could hardly wait to drop the needle and immerse himself in the music.

He embarked on a pilgrimage to Texas with just two suitcases and $500 in his bank account. His goal was to dive into the vibrant music scene and learn from fellow songwriters. Austin, known as the "Live Music Capital of the World," offered countless opportunities for him to grow as an artist. Open mics and songwriters' nights became his training ground, where he soaked up every moment, listening to others share their stories through music.

These days, he resides in Sonoma County, California, working hard as a touring artist and singer-songwriter for his original rock band, The Heartsleeves. He invites everyone to join him on this musical journey, sharing his songs one person at a time in this vast and unpredictable world we live in.

“Scott Ray Laws is an unique and really cool songwriter…he digs into materials, tells a story in his songs, and has a clean baritone vocality that is easy on the ears. We had a chance to meet and hang with Scott back in May ..and I HAD to have him back for a Wednesday evening.” Luigi- Owner-The Listening Room.

“..An ORIGINAL songwriter who knows how to tell a story clearly in song” -  Scotty O’Neill - Guitarist/Promoter

“ It was such a treat catching your set last night — really refreshing to hear something new and original. Thanks for pulling up a chair and hanging out with us — we really enjoyed the conversation and the stories behind your songs.”  -Tripp B. - Sonoma Songwriter

“Expect slow burning passion and vivid music …the kind of energy that turns into “let’s stay for just one more!..”  - Doug- Owner/Wine Maker- Spicy Vines

“...His lyrics simply tell first-person stories from his own life. Nothing fancy, he's not writing to impress--he pours himself, as is, into each phrase and melody.”- Rebecca Roudman- Dirty Cello Radio Hour KRCB Radio 104.9 FM

“ It is through forthright lyrics that are personal and earnest, that he composes lyrical pictures. Taking snapshots from the most common walks of life...”  - David Sampson - Producer Studio Secti West

“..relaxed mid-tempo Americana, capturing in each song the rhythmic pocket Laws is known for creating.” -  Coyote Music Review 2024

description:

title: Poetry Month Writing & Printing Workshop Series
description:
Each week, we’ll warm up with guided poetry prompts and group workshopping, then move into spontaneous composition using movable metal and wood type. You’ll set short poems by hand, experiment with layout and typography, and print your work on the press—embracing the beautiful constraints and surprises of letterpress.

As the weeks progress, we’ll curate and print a collaborative chapbook featuring original poems from everyone in the group. The final result will be a shared, tactile publication that reflects a month of creative exchange, ink-stained hands, and collective storytelling.

No prior letterpress or poetry experience is required—just curiosity, openness, and a willingness to play with language and form. Whether you’re a seasoned poet or brand new to writing, this workshop offers space to experiment, connect, and make something meaningful together.

*All materials included. Participants will receive copies of the finished chapbook.*

Join The Floathouse for a magical evening paddle on the Petaluma River—Petaluma’s Longest Park—timed to catch the full moon rising over the wetlands just south of downtown. As twilight fades, we’ll head out together in Hobie pedal kayaks for a relaxed, guided glide that turns nighttime into playtime.

These pedal-powered kayaks make the journey smooth and easy, even if there’s a breeze or moving tide. We’ll cruise about a mile and a half downriver to the perfect moonrise vantage point, where calm water, wide skies, and glowing reflections set the scene.

This is a social, feel-good outdoor experience designed for anyone looking for something a little different to do after dark—part nature, part adventure, part pure vibe.

$60 per person includes everything: • Hobie pedal kayak • PFD and safety lights • Experienced local guide • A memorable, moonlit river experience

✨ Easy. Playful. Peaceful. Spend your evening under the full moon—on the water.

title: Patton Oswalt: Effervescent
description:
April 1, 2026
PURCHASE TICKETS HERE
Doors 7pm/ Show 8pm
Ages: 12+
Patton Oswalt continues to leave his distinctive imprint across all areas of entertainment, from his award-winning comedy specials to his many guest roles on television. His most recent comedy special We All Scream (which also marked his directorial debut) launched on Netflix last September and Oswalt was recently nominated for a Grammy for his comedy album. Last year, he starred in the Magnolia Pictures comedy I Love My Dad, winner of the Grand Jury and Audience awards at the 2022 SXSW Film Festival.
Oswalt was nominated for a Critics Choice Award for his performance in Jason Reitman’s film Young Adult, starring opposite Charlize Theron. In 2009, he also received critical acclaim for his performance in Robert Siegel’s Big Fan; the film was nominated for an Independent Spirit Award and Oswalt earned a Gotham Award nomination for his performance.
Oswalt has appeared in many films, including The Circle, alongside Tom Hanks, The Secret Life of Walter Mitty and Zoolander, both directed by Ben Stiller, Steven Soderbergh’s The Informant with Matt Damon, and alongside Seth Rogen in Jody Hill’s Observe and Report, as well as Paul Thomas Anderson’s Magnolia and Todd Phillips’ Starsky and Hutch.
Oswalt’s past television work includes memorable roles on Parks and Recreation, which brought him a TV Critics Choice Award, A.P. Bio, Veep, United States of Tara, Seinfeld (his TV acting debut), and many more. He is also very well known for playing ‘Spence’ on The King of Queens for nine seasons. Oswalt is also the narrator on ABC’s hit comedy The Goldbergs. He provided the voice for ‘Remy’ the rat in Pixar’s Oscar® winner Ratatouille, and his other voice credits include ‘Max’ in The Secret Life of Pets 2, Sorry To Bother You, the SYFY series Happy!, Rick and Morty, Archer, and BoJack Horseman.
In 2020, Oswalt’s Emmy-nominated Netflix special I Love Everything was widely applauded upon release, and he received a Grammy nomination for his comedy album of the same name. In 2017, he received Grammy and Emmy nominations for his album and Netflix special Annihilation, which addresses his own devastating loss and dealing with the unexplainable, while making it all painfully funny. In 2016, he won the Emmy for ‘Outstanding Writing for a Variety Special’ for his sixth comedy special Talking for Clapping and a Grammy Award in 2017 for his comedy album. He has been nominated for a total of six Grammys and four Emmys. Oswalt has shot eight TV specials and released seven critically acclaimed albums — in 2009, Patton received his first Grammy nomination for his album My Weakness Is Strong.

title: Triduum and Easter Celebrations
description:
As we approach the highest holy days of the Christian year, we warmly invite you to join St. Columba’s, Inverness for the celebration of the Sacred Triduum, culminating in the joy of Easter Sunday. The Triduum \(Latin for “three days”\) is one continuous liturgy unfolding over Maundy Thursday, Good Friday, and the Great Vigil of Easter. Together, these services celebrate the history of salvation from Creation to Redemption. A history of Love poured out, suffering faced with courage, death held in hope, and new life in the most unexpected of places.

All services are open to the public.

Maundy Thursday – April 1 | 8:00 pm

Liturgy & Washing of the Feet

We gather to remember Jesus’ final meal with his friends and his commandment to love through humble service. The washing of feet invites us into vulnerability, care, and shared humanity.

Good Friday – April 2 | 12:00 pm & 3:00 pm

12:00 pm – Outdoor Ecological Way of the Cross

We walk together outdoors, praying with creation and reflecting on suffering, grief, and our shared responsibility for the healing of the earth.

3:00 pm – Veneration of the Cross \(in the nave\)

A solemn and spacious liturgy where we honor the mystery of the cross and the depth of Christ’s love.

Holy Saturday – April 3 | 8:00 pm

The Great Vigil of Easter & Celebratory Reception

Beginning in darkness, we tell the great stories of salvation, light the new fire, renew baptismal promises, and proclaim the Resurrection. A celebratory reception follows as we rejoice together.

Easter Sunday – April 4 | 10:00 am

Liturgy of the Resurrection & Easter Brunch

We celebrate the triumph of life over death, hope over despair, and love over fear. Easter Brunch follows. Come and feast with us.

If you are longing for meaning, beauty, or hope in these dark days, you belong here. Come as you are. Bring a friend. Walk with us from the table to the cross and the empty tomb.

description:

title: What About Age? Art Exhibit
description:
*What About Age?* art exhibit has arrived in Marin County! Originally displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows, this exhibit explores ageism through contemporary art, featuring works by both local youth and senior artists.

*What About Age?* is an art exhibit and educational initiative designed to challenge stereotypes about aging, address ageism and social isolation, and promote intergenerational dialogue through the lens of art.

In partnership with Youth in Arts, the exhibit features artworks by local youth and senior artists, showcasing how age intersects with creativity, identity, and experience. Under the guidance of Youth in Arts, these emerging and established artists work side by side to create collaborative pieces, fostering meaningful connections between generations and reflecting the exhibit’s core message: art is ageless.

The exhibit also includes artwork panels by New York-based writer and illustrator Aubrey Hirsch, first displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows and originally organized by Stacey Gordon, NYU’s Program Director of Next Phase Adult Caregiving and Retirement at Work Life.

The new exhibition will be on view at the Marin County Civic Center galleries from January 26 to May 6, 2026. Works will be displayed on the first and third floor exhibits, Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

The *What About Age?* art exhibit is presented by Marin Cultural Association in partnership with Marin Community Foundation and Youth in Arts. Beyond the art exhibit, the *What About Age?* initiative offers programming, led by Vivalon, designed to challenge ageism and provide resources for Marin County's growing aging population.

title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

**APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE**

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.”

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net**

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

description:
Instructor: Suzanne Carson

Thursdays 11 am - 1 pm

Beginning March 19

Fee: $30/Session/Ongoing

Drawing a Portrait is Challenging and Fun!

Portraits have always been my forte. I spent many years as a quick sketch portrait artist and later studied classical and impressionistic portraits.

This class will have projects and demos covering basic head structure and features, how to get a likeness and capture those qualities that make a portrait unique. We will also explore different portrait styles in art history.

Using photo references, we will begin with pencil and charcoal before using color. Students can work on their own projects as well. Beginning to advanced students.

title: Faye Dorman is the Featured Artist for April at Sky Ranch Gallery, Tomales
description:
My oil paintings explore the emotional, human landscape.

The malleability of oil paint allows her to layer color, to scrape away and rebuild and to let brushwork remain as a record of the hand and feeling behind it.

My years of being a therapist and sitting with faces that hold and reflect emotion is what I hope to capture in a portrait. I invite viewers to recognize their own internal world reflected back.

$25 – One Bag or Doll Entry $40 – Two Bags or Dolls entryTransform plastic dolls and create upcycled bags from trash into unique art. Join our hands-on Trashion workshop for the Gallery 212 Exhibit and Auction.

About the Class

This hands-on workshop invites participants to rescue and reinvent plastic dolls \(Barbies, Kens, and dolls that are under 12 inches\) often destined for landfills, where they can take 20 to 500 years to decompose. As part of Trashion Season, join us for the beloved Gallery 212 Exhibit and Auction \(April 3 – 25\) where discarded materials are transformed into small-scale works of art for a good cause. Together, we’ll reclaim these forgotten figures and reimagine them as expressive, one-of-a-kind artworks for submission to the gallery exhibit and auction. New this year: Bags! In addition to dolls, we’re expanding the exhibit to include bags—think totes, clutches, cross bagsm fanny packs, coin purses, and backpacks. Just like the Trashion runway, the only rule is that your piece must be made from unconventional materials and/or upcycled/used textiles. Participants will have access to access to sewing machines, hot glue guns, irons, hair dryers and other creative tools as well of a wide selection of trash and upcycled materials to bring their vision to life. BYOT \(Bring your own trash\) is also welcome and encouraged! The workshop registration is your application fee to the gallery exhibit! Come play, experiment, and collaborate while contributing to a dynamic gallery exhibit that raises funds for Sonoma Community Center programming through the auction. It’s a joy to see your art find a new home—and to be part of a creative community turning trash into treasure.

title: Forró Dance with Eric and Abigail
description:
Get ready to connect, spin, and glide to the irresistible rhythms of Forró! Originating in the Northeast of Brazil, Forró is a captivating partner dance known for its close embrace, playful steps, and infectious, feel-good music. It is a social dance that will enrich your life, perfect for a night out or a casual gathering.

You Will Learn:

The Basic Step & Close Embrace: You will master the foundational quick-quick-slow rhythm and learn how to comfortably and confidently navigate the essential close-hold connection that defines Forró.

Leading & Following Techniques: Discover the clear, subtle body cues required to effortlessly lead your partner through turns and variations, and how to follow with grace and responsiveness.

Traveling & Stationary Patterns: Learn fundamental steps like the ‘Caminhada’ \(walking step\) and common stationary turns that will allow you to dance on any size floor.

Rhythm & Musicality: Connect your movement to the distinct musical styles of Forró—from the mellow ‘Xote’ to the faster, more energetic ‘Pé-de-Serra.’

This class is perfect for anyone looking to learn a social partner dance, connect with Brazilian culture, and enjoy a vibrant, community atmosphere. No partner or prior dance experience is required! Just bring your enthusiasm and comfortable shoes!

Bring a copy of your receipt at check-in to Painting/Drawing Studio adjacent to Ceramics StudioJoin us for a monthly, heart-centered gathering where we come together to create Jizo guardians out of clay—symbols of compassion, protection, and peace. Rooted in the Buddhist tradition and echoed across many cultures, Jizo figures traditionally honor children and all who have passed, those in transition, and those in distress.This ongoing project is dedicated to remembering those lost to war, with a special focus now on the approximately 19,000 children who have perished in Israel and Gaza in recent years. Through the simple, meditative act of working with clay, we create benevolent beings that will become part of public exhibits and peace sites, offering spaces for reflection, mourning, and hope. Our gatherings conclude with a gentle ritual to honor the lives of these children.Located in the Painting & Drawing Room. The gathering is open to ages 12 - adult, and no prior clay experience is necessary—all clay and basic materials are supplied. title: What About Age? Art Exhibit
description:
*What About Age?* art exhibit has arrived in Marin County! Originally displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows, this exhibit explores ageism through contemporary art, featuring works by both local youth and senior artists.

*What About Age?* is an art exhibit and educational initiative designed to challenge stereotypes about aging, address ageism and social isolation, and promote intergenerational dialogue through the lens of art.

In partnership with Youth in Arts, the exhibit features artworks by local youth and senior artists, showcasing how age intersects with creativity, identity, and experience. Under the guidance of Youth in Arts, these emerging and established artists work side by side to create collaborative pieces, fostering meaningful connections between generations and reflecting the exhibit’s core message: art is ageless.

The exhibit also includes artwork panels by New York-based writer and illustrator Aubrey Hirsch, first displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows and originally organized by Stacey Gordon, NYU’s Program Director of Next Phase Adult Caregiving and Retirement at Work Life.

The new exhibition will be on view at the Marin County Civic Center galleries from January 26 to May 6, 2026. Works will be displayed on the first and third floor exhibits, Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

The *What About Age?* art exhibit is presented by Marin Cultural Association in partnership with Marin Community Foundation and Youth in Arts. Beyond the art exhibit, the *What About Age?* initiative offers programming, led by Vivalon, designed to challenge ageism and provide resources for Marin County's growing aging population.

$275 – Registration Cost $25 – Materials Fee $300 – Total Registration CostIn this six-week course, participants will learn a unique approach to watercolor, intended to alleviate the frustration that many experience when learning this beautiful yet challenging medium.

About the Class

In this six-week course, participants will learn a unique approach to watercolor, intended to alleviate the frustration that many experience when learning this beautiful yet challenging medium. We will focus on strengthening one’s observational drawing skills, giving the artist a foundation off of which to build their paintings in a step-by-step layering process that trains the artist to see value and color. Our subject matter will be flora and fauna – a sampling of plants and animals. These subjects are great for beginners and experienced artists alike; their organic shapes make them forgiving drawing subjects, but their beauty can be a muse for life.  Instructor Hannah Day is a passionate nature lover and watercolorist and will share her unique approach to rendering botanicals and animal portraits in watercolor. This class will work both from photographs and from life, practicing observational drawing in addition to watercolor technique. With six class sessions, participants will have the opportunity to develop their skills and build muscle memory with a medium that often feels like it has a mind of its own.  This class is open to artists of all skill levels. All materials are provided.

title: Art Exhibit: The Poetic Landscape
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  3/13/26

**APRIL EXHIBIT: THE POETIC LANDSCAPE**

EXHIBIT DATES:  March 30  – April 26, 2026

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.”

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net**

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Faye Dorman is the Featured Artist for April at Sky Ranch Gallery, Tomales
description:
My oil paintings explore the emotional, human landscape.

The malleability of oil paint allows her to layer color, to scrape away and rebuild and to let brushwork remain as a record of the hand and feeling behind it.

My years of being a therapist and sitting with faces that hold and reflect emotion is what I hope to capture in a portrait. I invite viewers to recognize their own internal world reflected back.

title: John Doe
description:
John Doe was born in 1977 when he arrived in Los Angeles. His previous life in Tennessee, Wisconsin & Baltimore was a great & fertile time but new music and social changes led him to events that created a life in art. He graduated from Antioch College in Baltimore in 1975, worked as a roofer, aluminum siding mechanic, and ran a poetry reading series. Ms. Meyers was his landlord in the rural black community of Simpsonville , MD.

John met Exene Cervenka at the Venice poetry workshop Nov 1976 and he started working with Billy Zoom around the same time. When DJ Bonebrake joined X in mid-1977 the line up was complete. They released six studio records, five or six singles and one live record from 1978-1993. Five of X’s records have been re-issued along with two compilations. The Unheard Music documents their lives and progress as a band from 1980-83. In 2009 the film was included in the Sundance UCLA Archive of greatest films of all time. They appeared several times on American Bandstand, Solid Gold and David Letterman. As one of the last original punk rock bands standing, they continue to tour. The day that X played a free noontime concert in Fullerton, CA, they caused Orange County’s greatest high school truancy rate to date.

In 1988 John started a family and lived in the Tehachapi Mountains, near the “Grapevine” of Highway 5, which separates southern and central California. He has recorded 8 solo records w/ numerous renowned singers and players, more recently including Patty Griffin, Dan Auerbach, Aimee Mann, Don Was, Kathleen Edwards and Greg Liesz. He has appeared in over 50 films and television productions, with some of his most notable roles in Road House, Georgia, Roadside Prophets, Great Balls of Fire, Pure Country and Roswell. He continues to act these days but more sporadically as his touring schedule has become more demanding.

Other musical side projects include work with the Knitters, Jill Sobule and The Sadies. He continues to write poetry and has even taught workshops from time to time. He currently lives in Austin, TX.

title: T-Bone N Weasel - Live Theatre
description:
The play follows the antic peregrinations of two ex-convicts as they make their erratic way across South Carolina in search of a hot meal or an easy mark.

Hoping to bring themselves up to at least the poverty level, two ex-convicts, T Bone \(who is Black\) and Weasel \(who is White\) have stolen a rather decrepit Buick and have set off across South Carolina with minor mayhem in mind. Moving swiftly from one adventure to another, they botch an attempted robbery,  are swindled out of the Buick by a fast-talking used car dealer, run afoul of a sexually voracious lady farmer, fall into the clutches of a larcenous country preacher, and try to make off with the automobile of a politically ambitious small town doctor who wants to exhibit them as examples of what poverty can do to people. Then it is back on the road again…

Every time they try to break the law, the law breaks them. A tale of two idiots, smartly told by playwright Jon Klein, “T-Bone n Weasel” is kind of like a good road-kill: it’s funny, gross and makes a lasting impression. — Variety

Her newest project, GLIMMER, is a collection of nine songs supporting one central theme:” Feel To Heal.” Within the grooves of the new album, Mae wrestles with the complexities of existing as a human with mental illness. From her \#MeToo-inspired feminist anthem “Warrior,” featuring a choir of 100\+ female vocalists, to “You Are My Favorite”, a love song written for her wife inspired by her own wedding vows which will surely be the 2019 wedding soundtrack for LGBTQ\+ couples, Mae shows she’s nothing less than a powerhouse. title: JaM Cellars Presents Y&T
description:
April 3, 2026
PURCHASE TICKETS HERE
Doors 7pm/ Show 8pm
Ages: 12+
Before Mötley Crüe, before RATT, even before there was a Metallica, Y&T was slogging away in sweaty rock clubs around America. When the band formed in the early 1970s, little did they know they would set the standard for hard rock bands that trailed. Many of the biggest acts of the ’80s became popular opening for headliners Y&T—and cut their teeth on the band, as evidenced by the Y&T mentions in tell-all books by acts such as Metallica and Mötley Crüe.
Born in Oakland, California, Y&T is one of the San Francisco Bay Area’s own innovators of the hard rock sound. Whether performing to a festival crowd of fifty-thousand or in an intimate nightclub, Y&T’s high-energy set and passionate performances still captivate legions of fans around the globe, proving Y&T’s music timeless.
Originally formed as Yesterday and Today, the initial powerhouse quartet—featuring Dave Meniketti (lead guitar/lead vocals), Phil Kennemore (bass), Leonard Haze (drums), and Joey Alves (rhythm guitar)—tore through the ’70s and ’80s with their own brand of hard rock. After two ’70s albums on London Records, they shortened their name to Y&T and released eight albums on A&M in the ’80s. Two more albums with Geffen Records marked an era of change with Jimmy DeGrasso (Alice Cooper, Suicidal Tendencies, Megadeth) on drums and Stef Burns (Alice Cooper, Berlin, Huey Lewis) on guitar.
With a discography of 18 albums, three greatest hits collections, plus a boxed set, Y&T has sold over four million albums since their 1974 inception. The band’s most recent single I’m Coming Home has climbed to roughly 1.5 million views on YouTube. Y&T received extensive airplay with hits such as Forever, Rescue Me, Mean Streak, Don’t Stop Runnin’, and Summertime Girls—which played in heavy rotation on MTV. Y&T songs have been featured in a multitude of movies and television shows, including Real Genius, Out of Bounds, Baywatch, and Hunter. After five top 100 albums, songs that tipped into the 40s, two Bammie Awards, and many international television appearances, Y&T’s hits are still played on VH1 Classic and classic rock radio stations worldwide.
With the passing of Kennemore, Haze, and Alves, it’s Meniketti who carries on the legacy that is Y&T. Y&T continues to tour the world, featuring the dynamic original frontman Dave Meniketti (lead guitar/lead vocals), John Nymann (guitar/vocals), Aaron Leigh (bass/vocals), and Mike Vanderhule (drums/vocals), playing songs that span the band’s five-decade career and including all the hits and fan favorites. Prepare to have your face melted.

title: Wreckless Strangers Live at Papermill Creek Saloon
description:
Thrilled that their newly released singles are getting national radio airplay and moving up the Top 100 Americana Singles and Top 100 AAA Singles Charts,**Wreckless Strangers** continue their album release celebration with several shows in the San Francisco Bay Area, including **Lucca Bar & Grill** in Benicia, the newly reopened historic **Papermill Creek Saloon i**n West Marin, a stint at the **Golden Gate Park Bandshell,** a fundraiser for **Challenged Athletes Foundation**, and more.

Wreckless Strangers return to their roots with their forthcoming studio album,*Dirty Souls*. The six-song collection marks the band’s rawest and most visceral effort to date — a modern take on the arena rock of the ’70s and ’80s that inspired their earliest musical influences. The first single, **"Dirty Soul,"** came out on January 23 and is getting radio play across the nation, and is available on most streaming platforms. Their second single, **“The Runaround,”** was released on February 27, and the full album comes out on March 27. Concert attendees will have the opportunity to purchase copies of the CD at the live shows.

***Dirty Souls*** is the band’s third studio outing under the tutelage of Grammy-winning producer **Dave Way**, who fosters a level of depth and organic cohesion that firmly establishes Wreckless Strangers in San Francisco’s storied rock ’n’ roll legacy. The songwriting is among their most intimate and personal, exploring themes of relationships, loss, empowerment, and perseverance. Co-lead singers **Amber Morris** and **David Noble** function as a single organism, bringing the songs to life with bluesy grit, soul, and humanity bolstered by rock-solid, road-hewn grooves.

Visit **WrecklessStrangers.com** and follow the band on social media for updates.

**Wreckless Stranger**s is a collective of friends and musicians carrying the torch for San Francisco’s grand rock ‘n’ roll tradition. Their unique blend of “Ameri-Cali Soul” melds the contemporary blues stylings of Bonnie Raitt and Boz Scaggs; the songwriting sensibilities of Sons of Champlin and Fleetwood Mac; the swashbuckling Americana of the Lost Planet Airmen and Peter Rowan; and the funk of Sly Stone and Tower of Power with a dash of Grateful Dead and Jefferson Airplane for flavor and unpredictability. With soaring vocal harmonies and burning instrumental improvisation, framed by concise, poignant original songwriting, Wreckless Strangers seek to honor and carry forth the brand of free-spirited musical fun and adventure that defines the Bay Area.

The band features **Amber Morris** on lead vocals; **David Noble** on lead guitar and lead vocals; **Joshua Zucker** on bass and vocals; **Mick Hellman** on drums and vocals; **Rob Anderson** on guitar and vocals; and **Fletcher Nielsen** on keys. The Rancho Nicasio show will also include special guests **Mike Rinta**(trombone), **Doug Rowan** (saxophone), and **Ryan Scott** (trumpet).

The band was recently invited back to perform live on Nashville’s famed Americana Roots radio station, WMOT, and performed at NAMM in Southern California in January.

title: Pt 1: Modifying Thrown Forms – Focusing on Teapot Making with Ping Zhong — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Pt 1: Modifying Thrown Forms – Focusing on Teapot Making with Ping Zhong

$10.00

Saturday, April 4, 2026; 10am-11amLocated in the Ceramics StudioIn this workshop, SebArts’ Ceramics Residency artist, Ping Zhong, will focus on the details and assembly of a teapot. Due to time and space considerations, wheel-throwing will not be demonstrated on site. Instead, pre-thrown pot bodies will be prepared as starting points. The workshop will center on shaping small components such as knobs, spouts, and handles, including hand-building techniques for forming these parts, as well as methods for attaching them harmoniously to the body. The instructor will also share practical tool tips to help participants work confidently with fine details and achieve a polished finish. This workshop is recommended to be held shortly after the instructor’s arrival.Due to limited capacity of the Ceramics Studio, we are asking for a suggested donation of $10 to confirm your attendance. About the Artist: Ping Zhong’s artistic practice is a continuous exploration of regeneration—of materials, forms, and cultural narratives. She investigates the dialogue between ancient Chinese pottery and contemporary visual language, using wheel-throwing, hand-building, and sculpture to create works in which history and personal growth converge. This reinterpretation of classical forms is not only an artistic method, but also a philosophical inquiry into the harmony between past and future. Deeply motivated to uncover the potential within clay, Ping pushes the boundaries of design and technique. Her work reflects on universal themes: the individual’s place within the community, the relationship between essence and appearance, and the evolving connection between nature and society. Through these explorations, she seeks to create art that resonates across cultures.

title: Park Rx—Intermediate Hiking for Fitness
description:
If you have previously completed the Beginner Hiking for Fitness Program, or can hike a little more than 4 miles with at least 1,000 ft of elevation, this hiking series is for you! The program leaders will guide you on 8 weekly hikes with the challenge increasing each week. Leaders will have group discussions about gear, hydration, hiking poles, first aid and pacing, etc. The group's final hike aims for Bald Mountain, where hikers can enjoy stunning vistas.

The following is a list of possible routes specifically selected for this hiking series:

1) Sat 3/7 — Creekside + Waterfall loop, 3.6 miles, 750 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 2) Sat 3/14 – Vista Trail loop, 3.4 miles, 830 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 3) Sat 3/21 – Goodspeed to Nattkemper bench, 3.8 miles, 1,240 ft elevation \[meet @ Goodspeed lot\] 4) Sat 3/28 – Hillside to Neptune table + Meadow, 4.4 miles, 970 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 5) Sat 4/4 – Hillside + Vista Trail loop, 3.6 miles, 1,070 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 6) Sat 4/11 – False Lake Meadow & Lake Ilsanjo loop in Trionne-Annadel SP, 6.1 miles, 670 ft elevation \[meet @ Annadel's Cobblestone Trailhead\] 7) Sat 4/18 – Fern Lake + Orchard loop in SDC/Jack London SHP, 5.5 miles, 1,460 ft elevation \[meet @ Walnut & North St inside SDC; park on Grove St\] 8) Sat 4/25 – Bald Mtn summit (w/optional Headwaters detour, 5.8 miles), 5.1 miles, 1,670 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\]

Please note these routes are subject to change based on the group and weather. Wear appropriate footwear for rocky or slippery trails, and layers. Bring water, and if desired, a snack. The group will be limited to 35 participants.

The hiking series costs $80 (plus a $10 parking fee per visit. Note that the Sugarloaf Annual Pass is $59 and valid at Sugarloaf and Jack London SHP), or free-of-cost for participants with a January 2025 or newer Park Rx from a Sonoma County Medical Provider.  The number of available Park Rx tickets is limited; please have your Rx ready at the time of sign up.

title: Summit Saturday: Gunsight Rock
description:
If you have previously completed the Intermediate Hiking for Fitness Program or can hike 8.5 miles with at least 2,000ft of elevation, this hike is for you! We strongly recommend completion of the shorter version of the Bald Mt. hike (in and out via Bald Mountain Trail) as a pre-requisite. This hike will be an approximately 8.5-mile point-to-point hike with 1900ft elevation gain and a short detour to Gunsight Rock. **This outing is not for children under 18 years old**.

We will meet at Hood Mountain Regional Park's Pythian Rd parking lot. From there, we will carpool to Sugarloaf's Goodspeed parking lot on Adobe Canyon Rd, where we will begin our hike on the Goodspeed Trail. Goodspeed has a major water crossing that is likely to have receded notably by April. Goodspeed turns into Nattkemper Trail at the Sugarloaf Ridge SP boundary. We will continue to Gunsight Rock and then to the Hood Mountain summit. From there, we will continue on the Summit Trail to Hood Mountain Trail to Upper Johnson to Pond Trail to Lower Johnson Ridge Trail, which ends at the parking lot on Pythian Rd. For those who left their car at the Goodspeed lot, we will carpool them back to pick up their car.

**This event requires registration**. There is a $10 deposit per ticket, which will be returned post-hike, unless you choose to donate it to support Sugarloaf. Wear appropriate footwear for rocky/slippery trails and layers. Be prepared for one slippery, major water crossing; we strongly recommend bringing water shoes, hiking poles, and an additional pair of socks. Bring your lunch, at least half a gallon (64oz) of water, and sun protection. Please note there is no water or bathroom access (except at the Pythian Rd parking lot), cell phone coverage (except in some spots along the ridge), or emergency services during this outing. Heavy rains cancel. Parking fees (Hood Mtn RP: $8; Sugarloaf Ridge SP: $10) apply.

**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on first, second and fourth **Saturdays of the month from 9:45 - 10:15 AM at** ​**Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin, 240 Channing Way, San Rafael CA 94903**. Contact: Sue M. 415-298-6792​. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, APRIL 4, 2026, 3-5 pm: Join us to meet KAREN MILLER and PHYLLIS RAPP;  celebrate the show and enjoy a poetry reading by featured guest, Linda Loveland Reid, gallery artist and published author.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthly drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.”

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net**

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

description:

These touching public events have inspired tears in even the most stoic audience members, as graduating guide dog teams proudly take the stage. Families are welcome at the ceremonies, which honor the independence and companionship that GDB’s guide dogs provide for GDB’s clients who are blind or visually impaired. The events also allow GDB’s clients to meet the puppy raisers who cared for their canine heroes prior to beginning formal training at GDB’s campus. Ceremonies also recognize recent graduates of GDB’s Orientation and Mobility \(O&M\) Program, K9 Buddy Program, and Breeder Dog Program.

Admission is free, and Kleenex will be provided. Pre-registered bus groups are welcome. Public tours of the campus are offered on the days of the ceremonies. Visit www.guidedogs.com for more information. Graduation events are also livestreamed at https://www.youtube.com/@gdb\_official/streams.

title: Ben Allison & Ted Nash & Steve Cardenas
description: Against the backdrop of over 25 years of creative collaboration, Ben Allison, Steve Cardenas, and Ted Nash weave musical conversations that are full of subtlety and surprise. They take turns arranging for the trio, which has released four albums. For this concert, they will be playing a selection of music from each of their recordings: Quiet Revolution: which features classics by Jimmy Giuffre and Jim Hall, Somewhere Else: which features our arrangements of songs from Leonard Bernstein’s West Side Story, Quiet Revolution: which features classics by Jimmy Giuffre and Jim Hall, Healing Power: which features music by the iconic composer/arranger Carla Bley and Tell the Birds I Said Hello: which features previously unrecorded gems by the genius pianist/composer Herbie Nichols. To date, their albums have been streamed millions of times, and they have performed at countless festivals throughout Europe, the US, and South America. The group is modeled after reedist/composer Jimmy Giuffre’s drummerless trios of the 1950s and 60s. As jazz was becoming more expressionistic and at times bombastic, musicians like Giuffre were going in the opposite direction. They were envisioning quieter music that maintained elements of blues and folk while also embracing the emerging qualities of free playing. Ben, Steve and Ted create music that is intimate and highly conversational in tone—a ‘musical trialogue,’ where group interplay is the focus.

title: Marty O'Reilly
description:
There’s something about Marty O’Reilly’s music that feels like it’s always been here—like an old story being told in a new way. His voice is raw and real, his guitar playing gritty and soulful. It’s music that doesn’t try to be anything other than honest, and that’s exactly why it hits so hard.

He pulls inspiration from the roots of Americana; his sound references folk greats like Woody Guthrie, blues legends like Howlin’ Wolf,  gospel pioneers like Sister Rosetta Thorpe, and master storytellers like Tom Waits. It’s a sound that captivates and connects audiences, and leaves them wanting more.

His live shows aren’t just concerts—they’re cathartic experiences. One moment it’s soft and haunting, the next it’s wild and electric. The kind that stay with you long after the lights come up.

But it’s not just about the sound. Marty’s songs dig deep into the human experience—loneliness, connection, love, loss. Whether it’s an intimate solo set or a full band show, he makes every audience feel like they’re part of the story.

Over the years, Marty has built a dedicated following through relentless touring and staying true to his craft. He’s shared the stage with artists like Shakey Graves, St. Paul & The Broken Bones, Sarah Jarosz, and Alice O’Donovan and played at festivals like Bottlerock, SXSW, and High Sierra Music Festival, but his focus has always been on making music that means something.

Marty has poured everything into his music—spending years on the road, self-funding his albums, and navigating the ups and downs of life as an independent artist, husband, and father. But through it all, he’s never lost sight of why he started: to make honest music that connects.

If you’re looking for music that feels real, that makes you stop and listen, Marty O’Reilly is someone you need to hear.

title: Monica Da Silva & Complicated Animals
description:
Monica da Silva grew up living between The United States and Belém, Brazil, a city on the Amazon River. A love of travel and foreign language helped to forge her unique sound.

Paralleling her life, da Silva's music contains an eclectic mix of Brazilian and American influences. Her sound can be classified as International Fusion, as it is heavily influenced by Brazilian music, namely Bossa Nova, but also incorporates elements of Lounge, Electronica, Indie Pop, and Worldbeat. Da Silva brings her cultural diversity to her songs, smoothly flowing between English, Portuguese, and Spanish.

In 2010, da Silva released her album "Brasilissima" . The record featured songs in both of her native languages - English and Portuguese. The first single "Aí Então", “was chosen by Putumayo World Music to be included on their compilation “Brazilian Beat”. The upbeat, psychedelic track "That's Not The Way" was chosen by the music director of ESPN to be played during the programming of The FIFA World Cup in 2014, alongside major recording artists Coldplay, Sérgio Mendes, Pitbull, Jennifer Lopez, The Black Eyed Peas, Stan Getz, and Astrud Gilberto.

Da Silva's single "Soldado de Amor" \(2017\) has been featured in the BBC One series "The Replacement”, in the Paramount Network series "American Woman", and in a 2019 campaign for the designer Tory Burch.

Her music has also been featured in the series "Heartland", and in an ad for Patron Tequila. She is currently recording a new, full-length solo album, as well as writing and recording with her project, Complicated Animals.

Sonoma County artist, **Karen Miller,** presents **The Poetic Landscape,** pastel paintings that convey Miller’s personal experience in connecting with the intrinsic beauty of natural places. In these pieces, color, fluid shapes and rhythmic design combine to create an uplifting mood – a true poetic interlude.  Evoking a happy mood, “Geyserville Sunflowers,” turning to the sun by nature, joyfully dance in its luminescence. By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.”

Meet the artist: Miller will be hosting the Gallery on March 30, April 5 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Phyllis Rapp’s Magic Moments,** a collection of watercolors that create an atmosphere that is both introspective and magical.  Familiar domestic scenes are transformed as humans interact with animals and birds in floral settings.  In “Silent Watcher” the red-headed young woman’s green eyes lock onto ours as she stares ahead, flanked by her avian companion.  Experiencing these works is a like taking a mini-step on the wild side, an exciting and fun experience.

Meet the artist: Rapp will be hosting the Gallery on March 30 and April 10 from 11am to 6 pm.

Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, April 2, 5 – 6 pm.  The theme for the 2026 kickoff event is Bouquets to Art.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: GLYPH  - Art Exhibition
description:

Big news! Personal Space is back from our \(much needed\) hiatus. Join us next Sunday, March 15 \(2-5pm\) for the opening of  Glyph. This is our first opening since Village opened up next door, and it’s sure to be a party!

Featuring thirteen artists from the Bay Area and beyond, Glyph embraces a liminal space which allows subconscious connections to reign and centers gut feeling as a source of poetry, mystery, and magic. title: T-Bone N Weasel - Live Theatre
description:
The play follows the antic peregrinations of two ex-convicts as they make their erratic way across South Carolina in search of a hot meal or an easy mark.

Hoping to bring themselves up to at least the poverty level, two ex-convicts, T Bone \(who is Black\) and Weasel \(who is White\) have stolen a rather decrepit Buick and have set off across South Carolina with minor mayhem in mind. Moving swiftly from one adventure to another, they botch an attempted robbery,  are swindled out of the Buick by a fast-talking used car dealer, run afoul of a sexually voracious lady farmer, fall into the clutches of a larcenous country preacher, and try to make off with the automobile of a politically ambitious small town doctor who wants to exhibit them as examples of what poverty can do to people. Then it is back on the road again…

Every time they try to break the law, the law breaks them. A tale of two idiots, smartly told by playwright Jon Klein, “T-Bone n Weasel” is kind of like a good road-kill: it’s funny, gross and makes a lasting impression. — Variety

Featuring:

Sponsored by Linda Hillel & Jon Eisenberg and Malin Giddings & Richard Hechler

**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on **Sundays from 4:00 – 5:00 PM** **at Christ Church United Methodist, 1717 Yulupa Ave., Room #4, Santa Rosa**. Contact: Abigail (707) 293-5888. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html .

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

title: What About Age? Art Exhibit
description:
*What About Age?* art exhibit has arrived in Marin County! Originally displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows, this exhibit explores ageism through contemporary art, featuring works by both local youth and senior artists.

*What About Age?* is an art exhibit and educational initiative designed to challenge stereotypes about aging, address ageism and social isolation, and promote intergenerational dialogue through the lens of art.

In partnership with Youth in Arts, the exhibit features artworks by local youth and senior artists, showcasing how age intersects with creativity, identity, and experience. Under the guidance of Youth in Arts, these emerging and established artists work side by side to create collaborative pieces, fostering meaningful connections between generations and reflecting the exhibit’s core message: art is ageless.

The exhibit also includes artwork panels by New York-based writer and illustrator Aubrey Hirsch, first displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows and originally organized by Stacey Gordon, NYU’s Program Director of Next Phase Adult Caregiving and Retirement at Work Life.

The new exhibition will be on view at the Marin County Civic Center galleries from January 26 to May 6, 2026. Works will be displayed on the first and third floor exhibits, Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

The *What About Age?* art exhibit is presented by Marin Cultural Association in partnership with Marin Community Foundation and Youth in Arts. Beyond the art exhibit, the *What About Age?* initiative offers programming, led by Vivalon, designed to challenge ageism and provide resources for Marin County's growing aging population.

title: Sonoma Mountain Cemetery Tour April 6
description:
Who provided 6,000 gallons of his own wine reserves to squelch the big fire of 1911 on East 1st Street? Who was pals with Jack and Charmian London and received birthday cards from several past and present U.S. presidents on her 100th birthday? Who created a whole new industry \(not wine!\) that brought thousands of tourists and dollars to the Sonoma Valley?

Learn about these and more personalities interned at the City of Sonoma Mountain Cemetery when the Sonoma Valley Historical Society \(SVHS\) inaugurates the Mountain Cemetery Tour on Sunday, April 6, 2025. Tour groups of 10-15 will be staggered from mid-morning to early afternoon. The groups will start the tour at the Mountain Cemetery water fountain \(look for signs upon arrival\). Parking available in the Overlook Trail and Veterans Memorial Building parking lots or on 1st Street West.

The cemetery is situated on the western slope of Schocken Hill and will therefore require tour guests to be capable of walking on steep terrain, wearing suitable walking/hiking footwear, bringing drinking water, and a walking stick \(optional\). The tour will last approximately one hour and fifteen minutes.

Cost: $20 plus fees. Space is limited; first come first served. There will be 3 groups at 10 minute intervals starting at 10:30 am To register for the tour

https://www.eventbrite.com/e/sonoma-mountain-cemetery-tour-tickets-1289131730709?aff=oddtdtcreator

Inquiries about the tour can be made at: info@sonomavalleyhistory.org.

SVHS is a 501\(c\)\(3\) non-profit corporation whose mission is collecting, preserving and sharing the story of our community as told by many voices throughout Sonoma Valley history.… Please visit our website at: www.sonomavalleyhistory.org .

By the river’s edge, concentric reflections conjure a calm sense of wellbeing in “Fetch.”  The viewer feels welcomed by a warm embrace entering a shaded secret spot in “September Trellis.”  Focused on local scenes, these works truly hone in on the stunning landscape out our doors.  Miller remarked “ As I contemplate the very real places of beauty surrounding us, I try to express my painterly response in hopes it will engender recognition by the viewers.”

Location: Santa Rosa Store

Join us for an inspiring gel printing workshop with Magdalena Bogart, where you'll discover the
magic of this versatile and expressive art form. You will learn techniques for creating stunning,
layered prints using gel plates, rich textures, and vibrant colors.
If you have wanted to try out this fairly new and very popular way to make your own papers, whether you are an experienced artist or simply curious about the process, this workshop will provide plenty of creative inspiration and expert insights.

During the 3-hours workshop, you will learn the fundamentals of mono-printing with a gel plate,
including an in-depth look at the essential supplies needed. Magdalena will discuss different
types of plates and brayers, as well as the wide range of acrylic paints and inks. You will learn the basics of color theory to ensure great results for your projects.

You will get to try out many fun techniques on different papers. Magdalena will introduce various papers for gel printing, including white copy paper, calligraphy paper, deli paper, marker paper, and more each offering unique effects.

The workshop will also explore tools for making marks and textures, from found objects to store-bought supplies. Magdalena will demonstrate how to use stencils - both handmade and purchased, along with unconventional tools like silicone scrapers, scrapers, bubble wrap, buttons, yarn, and cardboard to create stunning patterns.

She will also cover techniques to embellish your prints incorporating acrylic pens, Inktense pencils and other techniques.
Additionally, Magdalena will provide expert guidance on cleaning, caring for, and storing gel plates to ensure their longevity. To wrap up the session, she will showcase creative ways to use your printed papers, including ideas for collages, handmade cards, and art journals, along with a take-home list of even more ways to incorporate your gel prints into future projects. Whether you are looking to refine your skills or try something new, this workshop promises to be an engaging and educational experience. Come explore the endless possibilities of gel printing.

title: What About Age? Art Exhibit
description:
*What About Age?* art exhibit has arrived in Marin County! Originally displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows, this exhibit explores ageism through contemporary art, featuring works by both local youth and senior artists.

*What About Age?* is an art exhibit and educational initiative designed to challenge stereotypes about aging, address ageism and social isolation, and promote intergenerational dialogue through the lens of art.

In partnership with Youth in Arts, the exhibit features artworks by local youth and senior artists, showcasing how age intersects with creativity, identity, and experience. Under the guidance of Youth in Arts, these emerging and established artists work side by side to create collaborative pieces, fostering meaningful connections between generations and reflecting the exhibit’s core message: art is ageless.

The exhibit also includes artwork panels by New York-based writer and illustrator Aubrey Hirsch, first displayed at NYU’s Kimmel Windows and originally organized by Stacey Gordon, NYU’s Program Director of Next Phase Adult Caregiving and Retirement at Work Life.

The new exhibition will be on view at the Marin County Civic Center galleries from January 26 to May 6, 2026. Works will be displayed on the first and third floor exhibits, Monday to Friday from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.

The *What About Age?* art exhibit is presented by Marin Cultural Association in partnership with Marin Community Foundation and Youth in Arts. Beyond the art exhibit, the *What About Age?* initiative offers programming, led by Vivalon, designed to challenge ageism and provide resources for Marin County's growing aging population.

Watercolor Fundamentals - Part 2

This next series will build on what we learned in Part 1, quickly refreshing some techniques and then applying them in our paintings. We will create more complex landscape paintings, skies and seascapes; wet-into-wet and wet-into-dry nature studies in a few different ways, and we will venture further into painting from our imaginations. We will explore abstraction and non-representational styles, where we don't look at something and try to paint it, but instead work intuitively with colors and shapes and let the paintings emerge and evolve from there. You don't have to know where you're going, enjoy the journey and see where it takes you!

This class is designed for adults 18+

What you’ll do

What is printmaking? We invite you into our print studio to experience a fun beginner’s journey through this incredible art form in five paced weeks. Join Kelly in this unique introduction to print through the world of monotype, relief, intaglio and stencil screenprinting. This popular multi-session workshop is only taught twice per year in the spring and fall seasons. Students will try various techniques in this guided, hands-on class to create a beginning portfolio of prints. Learn a basic understanding of the four classic methods within the family of printmaking and gain access to our member’s print studio to continue working on your own projects. This class is perfect for absolute beginners or even experienced artists who may need a refresher course in printmaking.

Monotype – Create a single print on a flat matrix using ink and a variety of marks and  textures

Relief – Carve, ink and block print using a mini speedy carve block and a linocut tool

Intaglio – Draw, scratch and ink onto a surface to roll out a creative print using a small press

Stencil – Pull a silkscreen and learn to transfer a flat stencil to make a colorful printed impression

No prior printmaking experience is necessary. This class requires hand dexterity to maneuver carving tools and studio equipment. Students must feel comfortable handling machinery.
